query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a new many‐body potential that incorporates explicit, configuration‐dependent corrections (derived from ab initio liquid data) will better represent the multitude of atomic configurations in the liquid phase of multicomponent high-entropy alloys, substantially improving the phase‐space overlap between the reference and target systems over TOR-TILD’s conventional EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: A multicomponent high-entropy alloy (e.g., an equiatomic or near-equiatomic Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni system) in both solid and liquid states at temperatures near its high melting point.
generation.intervention: Develop and deploy an extended many-body potential – for instance, an augmented EAM or modified classical potential – that explicitly includes configuration‐dependent corrections calibrated against ab initio liquid data to capture the diversity of local atomic environments.
generation.conditions: Applicable for HEAs with 5 or more near-equiatomic elements at high temperatures (approximately 0.8–1.0 of the melting temperature) in both their solid and liquid states.
generation.structural_mediator: The improved potential function that includes many-body, configuration-dependent terms acts as the mediator by more accurately mapping the ab initio liquid’s phase space.
generation.mechanism: By incorporating explicit corrections that account for the many diverse atomic configurations in the liquid, the new potential enhances overlap with the ab initio target phase space. This leads to a smoother thermodynamic integration pathway with fewer mismatches, as the reference potential now more accurately reflects the structural fluctuations observed in the ab initio liquid.
generation.predicted_outcome: Free-energy calculations using the new potential will exhibit a significantly reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to those based on TOR-TILD’s standard EAM references (an estimated reduction on the order of ~40%, though the precise magnitude remains to be calibrated).
generation.baseline: TOR-TILD’s conventional approach using EAM references, which falls short in capturing the full configurational diversity of the ab initio liquid phase.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective in HEAs with near-equiatomic compositions at temperatures approaching their melting points. Its performance in systems with non-equiatomic compositions or at temperatures far from the melting regime is uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: Quantification of the improvement (i.e. the magnitude of the reduction in integration mismatch) is uncertain until detailed benchmarking against ab initio free-energy calculations is performed.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of thermodynamic integration free-energy calculations on a chosen high-entropy alloy system using both the baseline TOR-TILD EAM potential and the newly developed many-body potential. The experiments would run over a temperature range from about 0.8 Tm to Tm, comparing integration path mismatches, free-energy convergence, and phase-space overlap metrics.
measurements: Quantitative evaluation of the thermodynamic integration path mismatch (work/path smoothness)
Phase-space overlap metrics between the reference potential and ab initio configurations
Absolute free-energy differences benchmarked against ab initio free-energy calculations
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the many-body potential fails to yield a statistically significant reduction (e.g., less than a 10% reduction) in the thermodynamic integration path mismatch or does not show improved phase-space overlap relative to the TOR-TILD’s EAM reference, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Computational investigations of structural, chemical, and deformation behavior in high-entropy alloys (HEAs), which possess notable mechanical strength, have been limited due to the absence of applicable force fields. To extend investigations, we propose a set of intermolecular potential parameters for a quinary Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni alloy, using the available ternary Embedded Atom Method and Lennard-Jones potential in classical molecular-dynamics simulations. The simulation results are validated by a comparison to first-principles Korringa-Kohn-Rostoker (KKR) - Coherent Potential Approximation (CPA) [KKR-CPA] calculations for the HEA structural properties (lattice constants and bulk moduli), relative stability, pair probabilities, and high-temperature short-range ordering. The simulation (MD)-derived properties are in quantitative agreement with KKR-CPA calculations (first-principles) and experiments. We study Al x CrCoFeNi for Al ranging from 0 ≤ x ≤2 mole fractions, and find that the HEA shows large chemical clustering over a wide temperature range for x < 0.5. While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions. Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity. The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.
